Circles Lined On Tri Sides

GeometryCirclesTriangles
Game: Equal circles are lined up along the two short sides of a right triangle; watch how their size compares with the big circle inside it.
How to play: Drag the N and M dots, or focus one and use the arrow keys, to change the triangle. Press Show the R picture to see the big circle cut into small ones.
Look for the math

In an old Japanese temple puzzle, or sangaku, eight equal circles fit on the sides of a 3-4-5 triangle. The circle inside the triangle turns out to be exactly three times as big. The same trick works for every triangle made from two whole numbers.

Two numbers make a right triangle

Pick two different whole numbers N and M from 1 to 8. The three lengths N² − M², 2NM and N² + M² always satisfy a² + b² = c², so they are the sides of a Pythagorean triple. With N = 2, M = 1 we get 3, 4 and 5.

The big circle and the little ones

For a right triangle, the incircle has radius R = (a + b − c) / 2. In these triples that is the whole number min(N,M)·|N − M|. The small circles have radius r = R / (2R + 1), so the big radius is always a whole number of small radii: R / r = 2R + 1. For 3-4-5, R = 1 and r = 1/3, which gives R = 3r.

Why exactly that many circles fit

Along a leg of length L, L + 1 circles fit: the end circles sit r from the corners and neighbours are 2r apart. Writing the slope of the triangle as h, the fit is exact: r·(h + L)/other + 2Lr + r = L. The two rows share the circle at the right corner, so the total is L₁ + L₂ + 1 circles — eight for the 3-4-5 triangle. The logic test checks this, the tangencies and the integer ratio for all 56 pairs of numbers from 1 to 8.

A quirk of the old drawing

The applet's own drawing code paints its second row at the same height as the first, so it repaints three circles instead of putting them on the other leg. The article describes circles on both legs, so this page follows the article. The little blue picture shown by "Show the R picture" is the applet's own illustration: one circle of radius R with 2R + 1 small circles of radius r lined up underneath it.

Try N = 4, M = 1: the legs are 15 and 8, and the big circle is 7 small radii across.
